title: Private cluster saturation and token-rate backpressure causing TTFT spikes — rapid mitigation and rollback plan
creator: Aisha Patel
impact: High: two enterprise private clusters and one Dedicated capacity pool showing 2-4x increase in TTFT and 30-60% drop in tokens/sec for short sessions; visible customer-facing latency and timeouts.
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 an enterprise finance customer reported sustained TTFT spikes in their private VPC deployment (us-west-2). Investigation shows a recent routing/policy rollout introduced a priority inversion in the multiplex scheduler: long-context requests are holding the forwarding path open and preventing efficient small-request batching, leading to queue head-of-line blocking and token/sec collapse. This ticket coordinates the rapid mitigation, validation, and customer communication across Hosted/Dedicated/Private boundaries.
reproducer_steps: 1) Deploy model variant 'redwood/open-3B-q4' in a private cluster with mixed session lengths (short prompts 8-24 tokens + long priming 2k tokens).
2) Enable route_policy=v3 with multiplex-priority and per-tenant fairness (the setting from rollout 2026-03-03).
3) Replay customer traffic pattern via loadgen: 70% short-chat, 30% long-priming at 120 rps. Observe TTFT and tokens/sec on worker GPU metrics.
4) Observe stale KV-cache eviction and prefetch starvation correlated with token/sec drop and queue latency increase.
diagnosis: Preliminary root cause: new multiplex scheduling heuristic (route_policy=v3) elevates long-context traces into a single high-priority lane. Because the scheduler uses a coarse token-budget window, short requests are repeatedly deferred, causing small-batch starvation and increased per-request TTFT. Secondary contributor: reduced aggressive prefetch budget in the private runtime build (config flag prefetch_budget=2 -> 1) introduced in the same release.
timeline_updates: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Received CUST-9912; customer reports 3x TTFT and spikes coinciding with last Thursday rollout.

2026-03-10 11:30 - Jonah Martinez (on-call SRE): Triaged; queued traces show multiplex queue depth at 1.6x baseline and token/sec falling 45% on short sessions. Linked logs: https://logs.redwood.local/CUST-9912/trace
2026-03-10 14:00 - Team sync: Agreed to canary rollback of route_policy=v2 for private clusters in us-west-2 at 15:00 UTC; prefetch config revert as fallback.

2026-03-11 02:15 - Canary applied (5% traffic): immediate TTFT improvement for short sessions but long-context throughput regressed on the canary worker; rollback paused to avoid impacting customers with bulk long-priming workloads.

2026-03-12 08:40 - Debug session: Identified scheduling priority buckets don't account for interleaved short/long mixed-fanout; designed fix: introduce per-shard aging and soft-preemption (PR created).
2026-03-13 10:05 - Hotpatch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1789. Canary for soft-preemption scheduled for 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC across private us-west-2 and dedicated-pool-3.
2026-03-13 12:30 - Customer update sent (Maya Chen): described mitigation plan, ETA for broader rollout 48 hours pending canary results.
actions_taken: Canary rollback of route_policy to v2 attempted (5% traffic) and observed mixed results; paused to avoid regression for long-context customers.
Disabled aggressive batching for private workers via ops flag 'batcher_aggressive=false' as a temporary measure in us-west-2 (low-risk change).
Opened PR #1789 to add soft-preemption and per-shard aging; included telemetry hooks to emit per-shard wait-time percentile.
Notified Dedicated capacity owners and scheduled a limited canary to dedicated-pool-3 after private cluster validation.
next_steps: Run 6-hour canary of PR#1789 in private us-west-2 with 10% traffic focusing on mixed short/long workloads and the customer's replay dataset.
If canary improves short-session TTFT without harming long-context throughput, promote to 50% then full rollout with 30-minute monitoring windows.
Add automated regression test to perf-suite: mixed-session-fanout with 70/30 short/long adherence and assert tokens/sec >= 85% baseline.
Coordinate customer follow-up and share runbook for private clusters to reduce operational noise.
resolution: Partial: temporary batching flags applied and canary for soft-preemption under way. Final resolution pending canary validation. If validated, merge PR#1789 and schedule full rollout with post-deploy monitoring alerts.
notes: This incident highlights drift between private runtime config (prefetch_budget) and hosted defaults; add pre-deploy config drift check to release checklist.
Consider adding per-tenant adaptive budgets to avoid global policy changes that harm small-batch workloads.
Follow-up: perform postmortem after stable resolution and include customer impact metrics and SLA credit decision if needed.
